findings.title: Fifteen straights in eight round runs are shorter than the two take-offs of the tightest possible round elbow (R = 0.5 D): no stocked fitting pair can be installed there

evidence.measured: Re-count of 159 round straights / 122 elbows (turn >= 10 deg, clean_path, take-off R*tan(theta/2)): 37 short at R = 1.5 D (the check's 36 + GYM), 27 at 1.0 D, 18 at 0.75 D, 15 at 0.5 D (a 2-piece mitre, the smallest elbow that exists). Round 1 counted 50 / 39 / 29 at 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.75 D, so the legs have improved but the hard cases are unchanged. Impossible even at R = 0.5 D (leg in vs both take-offs): DU-ERV-RISER-EXH v4-5 1.6 in vs 6.0; DU-ERV-RISER-SUP v5-6 1.7 vs 6.0 and v6-7 5.7 vs 6.0; DU-ERV-EA v0-1 2.9 vs 4.0, v3-4 6.5 vs 8.0, v4-5 2.9 vs 8.0; DU-ERV-OA v3-4 3.9 vs 8.0; DU-B-ERV-R-SAUNA-SUP v0-1 1.0 vs 2.0, v2-3 3.5 vs 4.0, v6-7 1.0 vs 4.0; DU-B-ERV-R-SAUNA-EXH v6-7 2.0 vs 4.0; DU-B-ERV-RET-TRUNK v0-1 2.5 vs 3.0; DU-S-ERV-HP-FEED v1-2 3.4 vs 6.0; DU-ERV-RISER-EXH v7-8 2.5 vs 3.0. Three of the 15 are start legs beside a plenum collar (which may carry a stub); 12 are interior legs between two elbows.
evidence.expected: Every straight >= the sum of the take-offs of the stocked elbow at each end; the absolute floor for any round elbow is centreline radius D/2, so two 90s need >= D between them (6 in on a 6 in duct, 8 in on an 8 in duct).

findings.title: The house cites IRC M1601 for duct gauge, sealing and support, but Minnesota deletes IRC chapters 12-24 and applies Minn. R. 1346 (IMC 2018 ch.2-15): the governing sections are IMC 603.4 / 603.9 / 603.10 / 603.18 and Minn. R. 1346.0603

evidence.measured: Minn. R. 1309 (revisor.mn.gov/rules/1309/full) states 'Chapters 12 to 24 of the 2018 IRC and any references to mechanical matters in this code are deleted and replaced with Minnesota Rules, chapter 1346, Minnesota Mechanical Code'; chapter 1346.0050 incorporates 'Chapters 2 to 15 of the 2018 edition of the International Mechanical Code'. The repo cites 'IRC M1601' in six places (library/hvac.py:149, takeoff/mep.py:151, duct_sizing.py:178, model/air_products.py:32, inspections.py:158 code_refs, notes §11). The numbers are the same: IMC 2018 Table 603.4 (up.codes Minnesota IMC 2018 ch.6) rectangular 1/2 in w.g.: <=8 0.013, 9-10 0.013, 11-12 0.016, 13-16 0.019, 17-18 0.019, 19-20 0.024; round < 12 in 0.013 galvanized: the four DUCT-T-GALV-RECT rows (10 -> 30 ga, 12 -> 28 ga, 18 -> 26 ga, 20 -> 24 ga) match. What changes is the clause an inspector reads: 603.9 (joints, UL 181B), 603.10 (SMACNA supports), 603.12 (condensation), 603.18 (volume dampers with access) and the Minnesota amendment 1346.0603 subp. 10 (dampers adjusted and locked; a friction register box allowed where inaccessible).
evidence.expected: Citations to Minn. R. 1346 / IMC 2018 603.x, with the Minnesota amendments.

findings.title: Round duct gauge has three answers: library names 26 ga for 4/6/8 in, the note says the code minimum is 30 ga, and the takeoff prints no gauge for any round run

findings.title: The laying-length check grades every round elbow as a SMACNA gored R = 1.5 D elbow, but the BOM buys stamped/adjustable elbows and no source in the repo gives their radius or laying length

evidence.measured: library/fittings.py:222-241 makes `FIT-DUCT-{90,45,30}-{3..12}` 'gored elbow' rows with bend_radius_in = 1.5 x size and no center_to_face; `_takeoff_in` (fitting_pattern.py:101) turns that into R*tan(theta/2). prices.toml bills 'elbow-90-4in = 4 in stamped adjustable galvanized elbow' and 'elbow-90-8in = SupplyHouse 26 ga adjustable'. A retailer listing for the 4 in 30 ga adjustable 90 (Imperial GVL0028-A, lowes.com) gives a listed length of 6.875 in: the axis intersection is then 6.875 - 2 = 4.9 in from each arm end, so with a 1.25-2 in crimp stub the effective centreline radius is about 3-3.6 in (0.75-0.9 D), not 6 in. At R = 1.5 D, 37 straights fail; at 0.75 D, 18 (M4-101). No manufacturer submittal for a stamped or adjustable 4/6/8 in elbow was found (retail pages for Hart & Cooley, Snappy, Master Flow returned 403/no dimensions). Also: an adjustable elbow makes 0-90 deg only, so the 95.3 deg turn of DU-B-ERV-R-GYM (M1-008) cannot be one fitting.
evidence.expected: The catalog row names the part that is bought (adjustable 4-piece or die-stamped, by gauge) with its published laying length, and the check uses that.

findings.title: The disc-valve spigot is specified with 'UL 181A-P foil tape'; UL 181A is the fibrous-glass class, metal duct takes UL 181B (B-FX tape, B-M mastic)

evidence.measured: notes §2 reads 'mastic and UL 181A-P foil tape, no adapter' for the 98 mm spigot into the 4 in collar; §7 lists Nashua 324A as 'UL 181A-P/B-FX' (it is the B-FX listing that matters). IMC 2018 603.9 (up.codes Minnesota IMC 2018): 'Tapes and mastics used to seal fibrous glass ductwork shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 181A ... marked 181 A-P ... Tapes and mastics used to seal metallic and flexible air ducts ... shall comply with UL 181B and shall be marked 181 B-FX for pressure-sensitive tape or 181 B-M for mastic.' IMC 603.9's exception (no extra closure for locking-type seams below 2 in w.c.) does not extend to snap-lock outside conditioned space; every run here is inside, so the house's mastic/tape on every joint is a deliberate extra that no set page states (M4-104).
evidence.expected: 'UL 181B-FX tape or 181B-M mastic' on every metal joint, spigot and take-off.
evidence.method: read notes/air_distribution_products.md §2, §7, §11; IMC 2018 603.9 text in scratchpad src/imc6.txt.

findings.proposed_fix: Change 181A-P to 181B-FX/B-M in §2 and in the product source string; print it once on M-10x.
